meta.title: Writing and the LLM benchmark
meta.description: Fabio Akita's writing on AI: the LLM Benchmark v4 with 44 models ranked on a sabotaged Rails app, how he runs coding agents, and what the hype gets wrong.

hero.title: Everything I learn about AI, written down
hero.lede: I have blogged since 2006. These days most of it is about working with LLMs: what works, what it costs, and what is marketing. Every post is published in English and Portuguese.

benchmark.title: Every major model, tested on the same sabotaged app
benchmark.text: Version 4 is one Rails app that grows over seven sprints while an isolated subagent plants fourteen sabotages based on real CVEs. Models are ranked by vigilance: did they notice what was broken and fix it? I rebuilt the benchmark from scratch for the third time to get there.
benchmark.current: When a major frontier model ships, it runs through the same table. The latest round added {n} models on {date}. That is how I pick which model to use for what, and what each one costs per task.
benchmark.chartAlt: Bubble chart of the v4 results: dollar cost on a logarithmic horizontal axis against score, bubble size is wall-clock time, color is the harness. The best deals sit high and to the left.
benchmark.chartCaption: Cost against score for the Tier A models with a real dollar cost, from Part 2. Up and to the left is better; smaller bubbles finished faster.
benchmark.teaser: One Rails app, fourteen sabotages based on real CVEs, and {n} models ranked by whether they notice and fix what is broken. Every major new model goes through the same table.

benchmarks.title: Benchmarks
